description: cleveref: the type name is generated from the TARGET's environment, lowercase mid-sentence — 'lemma 2.9'
cleveref + a page hint; the page has no referent once the document is markdown, so this renders exactly as \cref
hyperref's own name table rather than cleveref's; always capitalized
renders the target's TITLE text, which the numbering walk does not capture (it would need brace-matched section titles) — degrades to the \Cref form rather than emitting nothing
a SPAN of two labels, not a list — 'theorems 2.1 to 2.5'
amsmath equation reference, rendered '(3)'. Resolved by its own pass BEFORE the generic dispatcher, so it is listed here only for usage reporting — never dispatched generically
the plain cross-reference: number only. Papers that want a type word type it themselves ('Definition \ref{def:x}'), which is why these sites already read correctly
cleveref's DELIBERATE bare form — number only, no type name. Rendering a type here would contradict the author's explicit choice
addresses a page markdown does not have; degrades to the target's number rather than emitting a fabricated page
